Every Labeled Effect in a Term, Including Its Sub-Terms

Source: R/blocks.R
label_pieces.Rd

Returns one piece per labeled random effect reachable from a term: the term itself where it carries a label, and the sub-terms developing its own parameters otherwise, walked to any depth.

Usage

label_pieces(
  term,
  param,
  nm,
  within = NULL,
  path = character(0),
  structural = NULL
)

Arguments

term

One built term.

param

The distribution parameter to which its equation belongs.

nm

The equation-level term's name, by which the design is keyed.

within

The piece's columns in that term's block, or NULL at the top level, where the piece is the whole of it.

path

Which of the parent's parameters were developed to reach the piece, outermost first, empty at the top level. It identifies the quantity on which the effect acts: a labeled random intercept written inside seg(x, psi ~ ...) is an effect on the break-point and not on the mean, and a report naming only the equation would be read as the second.

structural

Whether within indexes a structural term's own parameters rather than columns of the design. NULL at the top level, where it is read from the term; a recursive call passes the value that it received.

Value

A list of pieces, each with param, term, within, path, dim, tag, group (as modelterms7::term_group() returns it), structural and distrib. The list is empty if nothing under the term is labeled.

Why a sub-term is reachable at all

seg(x, psi ~ random(~ 1 | u | id)) develops a break-point over a labeled random effect. The labeled term is not one of the equation's terms (the equation carries one SegTerm, whose own label is absent), and its coefficients are columns of that term's block. They are the columns that modelterms7::term_components() reports as that component's sub_index, so a piece records them as within, positions in the parent's block, and the design turns them into positions in the stacked vector as it does for any other term.

A labeled effect written in a subformula of an additive term lives in the same vector as one written in an equation, so the same positions apply.

A structural parent addresses its coefficients differently: they are the term's own parameters, which contribute no design column and live in the design's structural state. The walk is the same and the positions that it composes are the same numbers (for a labeled effect inside gas(kappa1 ~ 1 + random(~ 1 | u | g)) they are the cols at which the unlabeled sub-term's own penalty is read), so a piece records which vector the positions index and not a different arithmetic.

Depth

A sub-term is an ordinary term and may develop parameters of its own, so the walk recurses and composes within on the way down: a depth-two sub-term's columns are positions in its parent's block, which are themselves positions in the equation-level term's.

A labeled term's own sub-terms are not walked. Its columns are the class's already, and anything inside it belongs to that block rather than to another.

See also

statmod_classes(), its caller; class_pieces() for the mapping of within onto the stacked vector.
